title: Feasibility of workplace-related collection and evaluation of biomonitoring measurements to assess exposure to hazardous substances
summary: Biomonitoring involves analysing blood or urine samples to measure the uptake of hazardous substances in the body. The study is monitoring at least three workplaces of varying sizes to see how occupational health doctors implement such biomonitoring on a group basis in their day-to-day work, with the aid of practical guidance materials. To this end, they independently collect between 10 and 30 samples per area of activity to test data collection and evaluation for comparable workplaces. The aim is to identify practical obstacles, develop practical guidance and support the further development of the regulatory framework.
conditions: The use of biomonitoring to provide objective assessments of workplace conditions

interventions.name: The study investigates the feasibility of biomonitoring measurement strategies under real workplace conditions. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The company’s willingness to support the company doctor in organising the sampling in accordance with the measurement plan.
▪ The supervising doctors to assume responsibility for the sampling.
▪ Carrying out biomonitoring with the aim of conducting a group assessment of employees with similar levels of exposure
▪ Compliance with legal requirements regarding data protection and the protection of the personal rights of employees participating in biomonitoring.
Exclusion criteria:
The supervising doctor is not prepared to carry out biomonitoring independently as part of a group assessment.
▪ No exposure to hazardous substances for which biomonitoring is possible.
▪ During preliminary discussions, foreseeable resistance to the study from employee representatives, the employer or occupational health and safety stakeholders
